{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjYzMjYyOTQ=","is_bot":false,"login":"anchapin","name":"Alex Chapin"},"body":"**Focus area**: Routing Intelligence
**PRD phase**: Phase 5 — Intelligence/DX
**Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
**Labels**: `bug`, `area:router`, `phase:5-intelligence`

### Problem
`containsWord` at `dsl.go:171-178` returns `true` for any string when `kw == ""`:

```go
func containsWord(s, kw string) bool {
    if kw == "" {
        return true  // ← matches everything
    }
    pattern := `(?i)\b` + regexp.QuoteMeta(kw) + `\b`
    matched, _ := regexp.MatchString(pattern, s)
    return matched
}
```

`regexp.MatchString("(?i)\\b\\b", "hello")` returns `true` (double word boundary matches at string start/end), so an empty keyword matches every prompt. If any `categoryKeywords` entry ever acquires an empty string, `Categorize` would return the first matching category for **all** prompts — silently corrupting routing for the entire judge-guided adaptive system. No test in `dsl_test.go` or `confidence_test.go` guards against this.

### Proposed solution
Return `false` when `kw == ""` instead of `true`:

```go
func containsWord(s, kw string) bool {
    if kw == "" {
        return false  // empty keyword matches nothing
    }
    // ...
}
```

Add a test case in `dsl_test.go` asserting `containsWord("anything", "") == false` and `Categorize("") != ""`.

### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `containsWord("anything", "")` returns `false` (not `true`)
- [ ] `Categorize("")` returns `CategoryOther` (not first matching category)
- [ ] Existing `dsl_test.go` and `confidence_test.go` tests pass unchanged
- [ ] `make test-race` passes with coverage ≥ 70%

### References
- `internal/router/dsl.go:171-173` — the buggy guard

1: // Package router decides where a request should be executed: local Ollama,
2: // frontier API, or both (fusion). Routing is two-tier: a cheap regex DSL
3: // fast-pass that handles obvious cases, and an SLM fallback that asks a
4: // small local model to judge complexity when the DSL has no opinion.
5: package router
6: 
7: import (
8: 	"fmt"
9: 	"log"

15: )

17: // Route names are the canonical string identifiers used across packages.
18: const (
19: 	RouteLocal    = "local"
20: 	RouteFrontier = "frontier"
21: 	RouteFusion   = "fusion"
22: )

24: // Default DSL patterns. These match the hardcoded behaviour prior to issue #305.
25: // Exported so the chat handler can fall back to them when the config fields
26: // are nil (e.g. in tests that construct config.Config directly).
27: //
28: // The patterns are compiled via mustCompileDefaultPattern (issue #588) so that
29: // an invalid default surfaces as a structured boot error (log.Fatalf) rather
30: // than a runtime panic from regexp.MustCompile.
31: var (
32: 	DefaultFormattingPatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
33: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("formatting", `(?i)\b(css|format|docstring|lint|typo|boilerplate|debug|fix bug|git commit|sql query|parse json|validate input|regex|api endpoint|test|optimize|readme)\b`),

40: 	}
41: 	// DefaultUnicodePatterns matches non-ASCII text categories (issue #422).
42: 	// Operators can override via NEXUS_DSL_UNICODE_PATTERNS.
43: 	DefaultUnicodePatterns = []*regexp.Regexp{
44: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("unicode", `(?i)\p{Han}`),    // Chinese characters
45: 		mustCompileDefaultPattern("unicode", `(?i)\p{Arabic}`), // Arabic characters

49: // compileDefaultPattern compiles a single default DSL regex expression and
50: // returns a descriptive error identifying the pattern group (formatting,
51: // fusion, local, or unicode) if the syntax is invalid. It never panics.
52: // This is the testable core of mustCompileDefaultPattern (issue #588).
53: func compileDefaultPattern(name, expr string) (*regexp.Regexp, error) {
54: 	re, err := regexp.Compile(expr)
55: 	if err != nil {
56: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("dsl: invalid default %s pattern %q: %w", name, expr, err)
57: 	}
58: 	return re, nil
59: }

61: // mustCompileDefaultPattern compiles a default DSL regex expression and is
62: // intended for package-level var initialization. On invalid syntax it logs a
63: // descriptive message (identifying the pattern group and the parse error) and
64: // calls log.Fatalf, so the proxy exits with a clear boot error instead of a
65: // panic (issue #588).
66: func mustCompileDefaultPattern(name, expr string) *regexp.Regexp {
67: 	re, err := compileDefaultPattern(name, expr)
68: 	if err != nil {
69: 		log.Fatalf("%v", err)
70: 	}
71: 	return re
72: }

74: // Guardrail returns RouteFrontier when the prompt is too large for the
75: // configured VRAM budget. The threshold is the maximum *estimated* token
76: // count the local model can safely handle. When maxTokens <= 0 the
77: // guardrail is disabled and ("", false) is returned.
78: func Guardrail(prompt string, maxTokens int) (Route, bool) {
79: 	if maxTokens <= 0 {
80: 		return "", false
81: 	}
82: 	if telemetry.EstimateTokens(prompt) > maxTokens {
83: 		return RouteFrontier, true
84: 	}
85: 	return "", false
86: }
87: 
88: // Route is a string alias for the routing decision. Use the Route* constants
89: // rather than raw strings so typos surface at compile time.
90: type Route string
91: 
92: // DSL runs the heuristic fast-pass. Returns one of RouteLocal, RouteFusion,
93: // or "" if no rule matched (caller should fall back to the SLM).
94: //
95: // fusionPatterns, formattingPatterns, and localPatterns are matched against
96: // the lowercase prompt (via toUnicodeLower) so that keywords like "REFACTOR"
97: // and "refactor" are treated identically. unicodePatterns is matched against
98: // the raw prompt because Unicode property escapes (\p{Han}, \p{Arabic}, etc.)
99: // are inherently case-invariant — lowercasing a Chinese or Arabic character
100: // is a no-op, and using the raw prompt avoids an unnecessary allocation.
101: func DSL(prompt string, fusionPatterns, formattingPatterns, localPatterns, unicodePatterns []*regexp.Regexp) (Route, bool) {
102: 	lower := toUnicodeLower(prompt)
103: 
104: 	if len(fusionPatterns) > 0 {
105: 		for _, re := range fusionPatterns {
106: 			if re.MatchString(lower) {
107: 				return RouteFusion, true
108: 			}
109: 		}
110: 	}
111: 	if len(formattingPatterns) > 0 {
112: 		for _, re := range formattingPatterns {
113: 			if re.MatchString(lower) {
114: 				return RouteLocal, true
115: 			}
116: 		}
117: 	}
118: 	if len(localPatterns) > 0 {
119: 		for _, re := range localPatterns {
120: 			if re.MatchString(lower) {
121: 				return RouteLocal, true
122: 			}
123: 		}
124: 	}
125: 	// Unicode patterns match non-ASCII text directly (issue #422).
126: 	// These patterns are NOT lowercased because they target script
127: 	// categories (e.g. \p{Han}) rather than ASCII keywords.
128: 	if len(unicodePatterns) > 0 {
129: 		for _, re := range unicodePatterns {
130: 			if re.MatchString(prompt) {
131: 				return RouteLocal, true
132: 			}
133: 		}
134: 	}
135: 	return "", false
136: }
137: 
138: // toUnicodeLower converts s to lowercase using Unicode case-folding rules
139: // (issue #422). Unlike the prior toLowerASCII, this handles all scripts
140: // (Chinese, Arabic, Greek, etc.). The allocation is proportional to the
141: // number of uppercase runes in s; prompts without uppercase return s
142: // unchanged (zero allocation).
143: func toUnicodeLower(s string) string {
144: 	if !hasUpperUnicode(s) {
145: 		return s
146: 	}
147: 	var b strings.Builder
148: 	b.Grow(len(s))
149: 	for _, r := range s {
150: 		b.WriteRune(unicode.ToLower(r))
151: 	}
152: 	return b.String()
153: }
154: 
155: // hasUpperUnicode returns true if s contains any uppercase Unicode rune.
156: // Used to skip the toUnicodeLower allocation for already-lowercase strings.
157: func hasUpperUnicode(s string) bool {
158: 	for _, r := range s {
159: 		if r != unicode.ToLower(r) {
160: 			return true
161: 		}
162: 	}
163: 	return false
164: }
165: 
166: // containsWord returns true if kw appears in s as a whole word/phrase,
167: // using \b word-boundary matching so that e.g. "test" does not match
168: // inside "contest". The keyword kw is already lowercased by the caller.
169: func containsWord(s, kw string) bool {
170: 	if kw == "" {
171: 		return true
172: 	}
173: 	// regexp.QuoteMeta escapes all regex metacharacters, then we wrap with \b.
174: 	pattern := `(?i)\b` + regexp.QuoteMeta(kw) + `\b`
175: 	matched, _ := regexp.MatchString(pattern, s)
176: 	return matched
177: }

3: // confidence.go closes the feedback loop between the async LLM-as-a-judge
4: // evaluator (internal/judge, issue #15) and the routing decision (issue #47).
5: //
6: // The judge scores ~10% of local-route responses on a 1..5 scale. Those
7: // scores were previously fire-and-forget. This file introduces a
8: // ConfidenceStore that aggregates historical judge scores by task
9: // category and exposes a single "how well does local do on this kind of
10: // task?" signal (0.0..1.0). The SLM router (slm.go) consumes that signal
11: // via DecideWithConfidence and nudges its system prompt toward frontier
12: // (low confidence) or local (high confidence).
13: //
14: // Dependency direction: internal/router does NOT import internal/judge.
15: // cmd/nexus/main.go owns both packages and bridges JudgeScore -> RecordOutcome.
16: // The confidence store lives here so the handler can call it without pulling
17: // in the judge package (the AGENTS.md hot-path dependency rule).
18: 
19: // NeutralConfidence is the confidence value that produces routing behaviour
20: // byte-for-byte identical to the pre-issue-47 path: no system-prompt
21: // augmentation. It is returned whenever there is insufficient data, the
22: // judge is disabled, or a query fails. 0.5 sits inside the default
23: // [floor, ceiling] band so the SLM request is unchanged.
24: const NeutralConfidence = 0.5
25: 
26: // Default confidence thresholds. When empirical local confidence for a
27: // category drops below the floor the SLM is biased toward frontier; above
28: // the ceiling it is biased toward local; inside the band the request is
29: // unchanged. Operators override via NEXUS_ROUTING_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR /
30: // NEXUS_ROUTING_CONFIDENCE_CEILING.
31: const (
32: 	DefaultConfidenceFloor   = 0.4
33: 	DefaultConfidenceCeiling = 0.85
34: )
35: 
36: // DefaultConfidenceMinSamples is the minimum number of judged outcomes a
37: // category needs before LocalConfidence reports anything other than
38: // NeutralConfidence. Below this the store returns 0.5 so routing is
39: // identical to today.
40: const DefaultConfidenceMinSamples = 5
41: 
42: // DefaultSuccessScore is the judge score (1..5) at or above which a local
43: // outcome is counted as "acceptable quality" when computing confidence.
44: // A 3 means "usable"; scores of 1..2 count as failures. This is a package
45: // constant rather than a config knob because the 1..5 scale is fixed by
46: // the judge's system prompt.
47: const DefaultSuccessScore = 3
48: 
49: // Category constants are the fixed set of task buckets Categorize emits.
50: // They mirror the DSL keyword spirit in dsl.go but cover the broader space
51: // the judge scores against.
52: const (
53: 	CategoryCSS           = "css"
54: 	CategoryRefactoring   = "refactoring"
55: 	CategoryDebugging     = "debugging"
56: 	CategoryTesting       = "testing"
57: 	CategorySecurity      = "security"
58: 	CategoryData          = "data"
59: 	CategoryArchitecture  = "architecture"
60: 	CategoryBoilerplate   = "boilerplate"
61: 	CategoryDocumentation = "documentation"
62: 	CategoryOther         = "other"
63: )
64: 
65: // ConfidenceStore aggregates historical judge outcomes by task category and
66: // answers "for prompts like this, does the local model deliver acceptable
67: // quality?".
68: //
69: // Implementations must be safe for concurrent use: RecordOutcome is called
70: // from the judge worker pool while LocalConfidence is called from request
71: // goroutines.
72: type ConfidenceStore interface {
73: 	// RecordOutcome persists one judged outcome. route is the route that
74: 	// produced the scored output (only RouteLocal outcomes influence
75: 	// LocalConfidence). judgeScore is the 1..5 judge rating; scores
76: 	// outside that range are ignored. An empty category returns an error
77: 	// so upstream callers that fail to categorize a prompt are surfaced
78: 	// rather than silently polluting the "other" bucket (issue #591).
79: 	RecordOutcome(category string, route Route, judgeScore int) error
80: 
81: 	// LocalConfidence returns the fraction of recent local outcomes for
82: 	// category that scored acceptably (0.0..1.0). It returns
83: 	// NeutralConfidence (0.5) when there is insufficient data so the
84: 	// caller's routing is unchanged. An empty category returns an error
85: 	// so upstream callers that fail to categorize a prompt are surfaced
86: 	// rather than silently coercing to CategoryOther (issue #802).
87: 	LocalConfidence(category string) (float64, error)
88: }

90: // categoryKeywords maps each category to the word-boundary-matched
91: // keywords that select it. Order matters: earlier entries win when a
92: // prompt matches several categories, so the list runs from most-
93: // specific/most-complex (architecture, debugging) to least
94: // (documentation) before falling through to "other". Keywords are
95: // matched against the Unicode-lowercased prompt using word-boundary
96: // matching (containsWord) so that e.g. "test" does not match inside
97: // "contest", ensuring consistent routing with the DSL \b...\b patterns.

109: 		"fails", "failing", "broken",

114: 	}},

117: 		"generate tests", "test case", "mock", "fixture", "coverage", "benchmark",
118: 		"assert", "pytest", "jest",

122: 		"auth check", "owasp", "cve", "exploit", "pen test", "sast", "hardening",
123: 	}},

126: 		"parse json", "data model", "etl", "analytics", "pipeline",

130: 		"rename", "clean up", "cleanup", "simplify", "deduplicate", "move method",
131: 		"reorganize",
132: 	}},
133: 	{CategoryBoilerplate, []string{
134: 		"boilerplate", "scaffold", "template", "getter", "setter", "crud",
135: 		"skeleton", "stub", "starter",
136: 	}},
137: 	{CategoryDocumentation, []string{
138: 		"docstring", "documentation", "document ", "readme", "comment",
139: 		"explain", "javadoc", "godoc", "changelog",
140: 	}},
141: }

143: // Categorize buckets prompt into one of the fixed Category* constants using
144: // a lightweight keyword classifier. It never calls out to an embedding
145: // model — it is a pure, cheap function on the prompt text so it is safe to
146: // call on the request hot path. Unmatched prompts fall through to
147: // CategoryOther.
148: func Categorize(prompt string) string {
149: 	lower := toUnicodeLower(prompt)
150: 	for _, group := range categoryKeywords {
151: 		for _, kw := range group.keywords {
152: 			if containsWord(lower, kw) {
153: 				return group.category
154: 			}
155: 		}
156: 	}
157: 	return CategoryOther
